cap: The HIV life cycle doubles as the antiretroviral map. Attachment needs gp120, CD4 and a coreceptor; fusion needs gp41; reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA; integrase makes the provirus permanent; host enzymes build gag-pol polyproteins; and the viral protease cuts them into a mature, infectious virion. Each drug class sits on the one step it blocks.
teach: Two features of the cycle explain treatment rules. Reverse transcriptase does not proofread, so every round of replication creates mutants and a single drug quickly selects a resistant one; that is why regimens combine drugs from two classes. Integration makes the infection permanent, because a resting CD4 cell can carry the provirus for years without making virus, which is why stopping therapy lets the viral load rebound.
